title: Config Sync plugin settings (data.json)
description: <vault>/.obsidian/plugins/config-sync/data.json at schemaVersion 4 — src/main.ts's ConfigSyncSettings, the plugin's OWN settings document (not the sync store). The sync list is never stored directly: it is COMPILED from `items` on every load/save (src/core/registry.ts's compileItems). Authority: src/main.ts (ConfigSyncSettings/DEFAULT_SETTINGS), src/core/registry.ts (Item/ItemMap), src/core/types.ts (Sharing/FieldRule/FileRule/Remote), src/core/switchList.ts (perElementKeyFor), src/core/enablementRules.ts (ruleHomeFor), src/core/settingsMigration.ts (CURRENT_SCHEMA) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's Data model section. `schemaVersion` gates everything: a document with a HIGHER number is refused outright (never downgraded, never overwritten) rather than validated against this shape — see settingsMigration.ts's classifySettings.

schemaVersion.description: Must equal settingsMigration.ts's CURRENT_SCHEMA. A document this build wrote always carries exactly 4; an older number is migrated on load (v2 -> v3 -> v4, never validated against this schema first), and a higher number stops this build from touching the document at all (invariant II.3) — this schema describes ONLY the v4 shape a current build reads and writes.

pkmMode.description: Which PKM framework convention decides the store's default root path (src/core/pkm.ts's PkmMode). "auto" detects the ioto-update plugin at runtime; "ioto"/"default" pin the choice. Part of the fleet-shared contract: unlike rootPath and remotes it carries no selfPresetRules strip (catalog.ts locks only those two), so it travels with config-sync's own settings — the resulting root path still differs per device only if a device overrides rootPath.

rootPath.description: Vault-relative path (no leading slash — e.g. the defaults "config-sync" and "0-Extra/config-sync") to this device's sync store root, or "" to follow the pkmMode default (src/core/pkm.ts's resolveRootPath). Locked-local transport wiring (catalog.ts's selfPresetRules, sharing: this-device) — every device may legitimately point at a different root, so this field is stripped from the self item's own store copy and never overwrites another device's value on pull/apply.

remotes.description: Configured sync remotes (src/core/types.ts's Remote union). Locked-local transport wiring like rootPath — a remote's URL/path/credentials describe THIS device's connection to the fleet, so this field never leaves the device either (catalog.ts's selfPresetRules).

ribbonButtons.description: Per-button ribbon-icon visibility (src/core/types.ts's RibbonButtons = Record<RibbonKey, boolean>). Unknown/future keys ride through untouched (invariant II.1) — see the schema-wide note.

sync.description: Show a dedicated ribbon icon that opens the Sync Center, separate from the plugin's always-present main ribbon icon.

statusInMenu.description: Show pending up/down counts in the ribbon icon's click menu title.

statusBarItem.description: Master toggle for the status-bar item.

statusBarRemote.description: Include per-remote push/pull count segments (⇡/⇣) in the status-bar item.

ribbonDot.description: Legacy corner dot on the main ribbon icon signalling pending changes; off by default since the status-bar item took over the same job.

mobileStatusBar.description: Force-show Obsidian's own status bar on phones (a CSS class toggle only; no data of its own).

remoteAutoCheck.description: Periodically refresh remote push/pull state in the background (desktop only — src/main.ts gates the timers on Platform.isDesktop).

localPeriodicCheck.description: Periodically refresh local (store-vs-vault) sync status while the window has focus.

sharing.description: "Who shares a value" (src/core/types.ts's Sharing) — a union, not a flat enum, because the device class only exists for one of the three answers.

oneOf.description: Every device gets the same value; the default reading when no rule mentions a key at all.

class.description: Which device class carries this value; the other class keeps its own value in a __scopes__ sidecar.

oneOf.description: Each device CLASS keeps its own value.
Never enters the store, never resurrected from it — a value or an enablement decision that stays purely local to this one device.

fileSharing.description: A file-level Sharing that excludes this-device (src/core/types.ts's FileSharing): a Plain file that should not sync at all is expressed by the item's own `synced` toggle, not by a file-level rule.

oneOf.description: Every device gets the same file content.
Each device CLASS keeps its own copy of the file; the other class's copy lives in a __scopes__ sidecar.

itemFieldRule.description: A per-key field rule as stored under `settingsFile.rules[<pattern>]` (src/core/registry.ts's ItemFieldRule = Omit<FieldRule, "pattern">). The map KEY is the key-name glob pattern (`*` wildcard) — deliberately not repeated as a `pattern` property here, so there is exactly one source of truth for which key a rule governs.

encrypted.description: Whole-value encryption for this key. A this-device rule can never be encrypted — nothing leaves the device for encryption to protect in transit — but this schema does not enforce that cross-field rule; src/core/manifest.ts's validator does.

locked.description: Preset rule injected by the plugin itself (e.g. the self item's rootPath/remotes strips); cannot be removed through the UI.

fileRule.description: Plain-mode whole-file rule (src/core/types.ts's FileRule), stored on `settingsFile.fileRule`. Only meaningful when `settingsFile.mode` is "plain" (or absent) — manifest.ts rejects it combined with "fields"/"encrypted".

encrypted.description: Whole-file encryption: the item's entire store copy is one encrypted envelope instead of the raw file.

perElementSharing.description: Element value/id -> Sharing, for one string-array (or on/off-map) key. An element with no entry here defaults to everywhere.

settingsFile.description: One item's own settings-file configuration (src/core/registry.ts's ItemSettingsFile). A registry item's `mode` is DERIVED from whether it has any per-key rules (never chosen directly); a `custom` item chooses it explicitly, "encrypted" included.

mode.description: "plain" = whole file, one rule at most (fileRule). "fields" = per-key rules (rules/perElement apply). "encrypted" = the whole file is one encrypted envelope; custom items only.

rules.description: Key-name glob pattern -> field rule. Only meaningful in "fields" mode.

perElement.description: JSON field key -> per-element sharing map, for string-array/boolean-map keys (src/core/types.ts's PerElementSharing, generalizing the switch-list mechanism to any such key). RESERVED KEY "": on the two carrier items ONLY — items.obsidian["core-plugins"].settingsFile.perElement[""] and items.obsidian["community-plugins"].settingsFile.perElement[""] — the empty string means "this whole file IS the list" (src/core/switchList.ts's perElementKeyFor): core-plugins.json/community-plugins.json have no JSON field to index a rule by, so their carrier item's rules live under this key instead of a real field name. Every other item indexes perElement by an actual field name (e.g. appearance's "enabledCssSnippets" — src/core/enablementRules.ts's ruleHomeFor: snippets rules live at items.obsidian.appearance.settingsFile.perElement["enabledCssSnippets"]).

companion.description: A companion folder riding an item's card (src/core/registry.ts's ItemCompanion) — a preset (appearance's themes/snippets) or a user-added folder.

path.description: Vault-relative path; may start with the {configDir} variable.

device.description: Which device class this companion group syncs on (src/core/types.ts's DeviceClass).

enabled.description: Whether this companion folder currently syncs (rides its owner's card). NOT the field the item-level `enabled` -> `synced` rename touched — companions kept the name because it never had the double meaning that forced the rename.

item.description: One item's stored configuration (src/core/registry.ts's Item) — the same shape whether the item is a registry item (an installed Obsidian card/core plugin/community plugin) or a `custom` rule. UNKNOWN PROPERTIES ARE VALID AND MUST BE PRESERVED: registry.ts's WRITTEN_ITEM_KEYS carries every field this build does not itself write through untouched (invariant II.1) — a field a NEWER build recorded here must survive an older build's round trip.

synced.description: Is this item synced at all. It never means "this plugin is turned on": that answer lives in Obsidian's own on/off-list files and is never stored here. `{synced: false}` is NOT residue to prune: an entry's mere PRESENCE in items.core/items.community is this device's capture mask for that on/off-list element, so an absent entry and a `{synced: false}` entry mean different things, and nothing on the write path removes an entry once written.

type.description: Required on a `custom` item (which has no registry def to derive it from); absent on a registry item, whose type is always "file" (its own settings file). v2's "dir" is converted by the migration and is never written or read as such by this build.

path.description: Set only when it differs from the item's registry default path; required for a `custom` item, which has no def to derive one from.

bratRepo.description: The BRAT repo this plugin installs from, "owner/repo" — cached here from BRAT's own list so classification (the Beta tab) and install-on-apply work without re-resolving. A property of the plugin it describes, not of BRAT: this replaced a v3 top-level `bratIndex` map, a second list of plugin ids that could drift from items.community the moment a plugin left one and not the other.

companions.description: Preset (themes/snippets) plus user-added companion folders. Optional and never written empty: an item earns its card whether or not it carries this field.

description.description: Custom items only — kept from the pre-v3 SyncGroup literal.

label.description: Custom items only — display name recorded at capture/enable.

origin.description: Custom items only. Set when the rule was created from the Discovered-files section; name/path are then fixed by the file.

itemSection.description: ItemId -> Item, for one storage section.

itemMap.description: The document's item store (src/core/registry.ts's ItemMap): StorageSection -> ItemId -> Item. Exactly two levels, NEVER flattened, and never a `beta` key — `beta` is a presented classification derived at runtime from each community item's own bratRepo (registry.ts's storageSection), not a storage key. Two ids may legitimately collide across sections (a core plugin and a community plugin sharing a name), which is the point of nesting.

obsidian.description: The three Obsidian cards (app, appearance, hotkeys) plus the two enablement carriers (core-plugins, community-plugins — real items since 2026-08-12-enablement-two-layers, not a compile-time-only artifact).

core.description: One entry per core plugin id this device has (or has had) an opinion about.

community.description: One entry per community/beta plugin id, including config-sync's own self item (catalog.ts's SELF_ITEM_ID = "config-sync") and every BRAT-managed ("beta") plugin — beta is a presented section only; it stores here.

custom.description: Hand-added rules for files/folders with no registry item — the Advanced tab's "Custom rules"/"Discovered files". `type` and `path` are required on every entry here.

remote.description: src/core/types.ts's Remote union, validated on write by src/core/manifest.ts's parseRemote (invoked from the settings-tab save path, not on every data.json load).

name.description: Display name for this remote, unique among this device's remotes; also the key run records and status use to say which remote a pull/push targeted.

type.description: A sibling vault's store on the same filesystem, reached by path.

storePath.description: Absolute path of the store directory on this device's filesystem, or a leading-~ path. Never a vault-relative path — this is a filesystem location outside the vault entirely.

excludeSelf.description: true = config-sync's own settings never travel to/from this remote. Absent = false.

name.description: Display name for this remote, unique among this device's remotes; also the key run records and status use to say which remote a pull/push targeted.

type.description: A git repository holding a store (desktop only — the git transport shells out to the git binary).

url.description: Clone URL (https or ssh), passed to git verbatim.

branch.description: Branch pulled from and pushed to; never inferred from the repository's default.

subdir.description: Store folder inside the repo; absent = repo root. Must stay inside the repository — the validator (manifest.ts's parseRemote) additionally rejects a leading slash and any ".." segment, and drops an empty string rather than storing it.

excludeSelf.description: true = config-sync's own settings never travel to/from this remote. Absent = false.

tokenId.description: Name of the keychain secret holding the access token — the token itself never enters data.json. Never the reserved id "config-sync-passphrase" (the encryption passphrase's own secret; manifest.ts rejects a remote that names it).

username.description: Sent alongside the token; absent = "token", which PAT-only hosts ignore but a self-hosted GitLab validates. Not offered in the settings UI (a linked token alone suffices in practice) but honored when present in a hand-edited document. The validator additionally rejects whitespace and control characters — the value enters a git credential-helper protocol line.

runHistorySettings.description: Retention settings for the run-history log (src/main.ts's RunHistorySettings) — configuration, not the log itself. These settings are ordinary shared fields and travel with config-sync's own settings like any other; the log file they govern (run-history.json, schema/run-history.schema.json) is what stays local to each device.

enabled.description: Master switch: record a RunRecord for every capture/apply/pull/push/removal run.
